title: Python Foundations
description: Learn the basic building blocks of Python including variables, strings, integers, and floats.

missions.title: Hello World
missions.description: Every programmer starts here. Forge your very first instruction to print text to the console.
missions.objective: Print exactly "Hello, World!" to the console.
hints: Use the print() function with double quotes around Hello, World!

missions.title: Variables Quiz
missions.description: Test your understanding of how variables are assigned in Python.
missions.objective: Which of the following is a valid variable assignment in Python?
hints: Variable names cannot start with numbers or contain hyphen dashes.

missions.title: Integers
missions.description: Learn how Python stores whole numbers using integer variables.
missions.objective: Create a variable named age with the value 18 and print it.
hints: Write: age = 18 followed by print(age)

missions.title: Floats Check
missions.description: Identify decimal data types in Python.
missions.objective: Fill in the blank to store a float value of 3.14 in pi.
hints: Enter just the decimal number 3.14

missions.title: Strings
missions.description: Create text variables using string formatting.
missions.objective: Create a variable named city with the value "Kashmir" and print it.
hints: Write: city = "Kashmir" followed by print(city)

title: Control Flow & Decisions
description: Master program logic using booleans, comparison operators, and if-elif-else conditional blocks.

missions.title: Booleans Quiz
missions.description: Booleans represent truth values in Python.
missions.objective: Which keyword represents a true boolean state in Python?
hints: In Python, boolean literals start with a capital letter.

missions.title: The IF Statement
missions.description: Use if statements to execute code only when a condition is True.
missions.objective: Create a variable score = 85. Write an if statement checking if score > 50, and print "Passed".
hints:
Write:
score = 85
if score > 50:
    print("Passed")

missions.title: Else Fallback
missions.description: Use else blocks to provide a fallback path when the condition is False.
missions.objective: Create age = 15. If age >= 18 print "Adult", else print "Minor".

missions.title: Elif Chains
missions.description: Chain multiple conditions together using elif (else if).
missions.objective: Create speed = 70. If speed > 80 print "Fast", elif speed > 50 print "Normal", else print "Slow".

missions.title: Logical AND / OR
missions.description: Combine multiple conditions using the 'and' and 'or' keywords.
missions.objective: Create age = 20 and has_license = True. If age >= 18 and has_license print "Drive", else print "No".
hints:
Write:
age = 20
has_license = True
if age >= 18 and has_license:
    print("Drive")
else:
    print("No")

title: Loops & Iteration
description: Automate repetitive tasks using for loops, range sequences, while loops, and early break statements.

missions.title: For Loops
missions.description: Iterate over elements in a list using a for loop.
missions.objective: Create numbers = [1, 2, 3]. Use a for loop to print each item in numbers.
hints:
Write:
numbers = [1, 2, 3]
for num in numbers:
    print(num)

missions.title: Range Quiz
missions.description: Understand range parameters.
missions.objective: Which numbers are produced by range(1, 4)?
hints: The end index in range(start, end) is exclusive.

missions.title: While Loops
missions.description: Repeat code as long as a condition evaluates to True.
missions.objective: Create count = 1. Write a while loop checking while count <= 3: that prints count and increments count by 1.
hints:
Write:
count = 1
while count <= 3:
    print(count)
    count = count + 1

validAnswers:
count = 1
while count <= 3:
    print(count)
    count = count + 1

missions.title: Break Statements
missions.description: Exit a loop prematurely when a condition is met.
missions.objective: Loop over range(1, 6) using for i in range(1, 6):. If i == 3 break, otherwise print i.

missions.title: Accumulator Pattern
missions.description: Sum values dynamically inside an iteration loop.
missions.objective: Create total = 0. Use a for loop over range(1, 4) to add i to total, then print total after the loop.
hints:
Write:
total = 0
for i in range(1, 4):
    total = total + i
print(total)

validAnswers:
total = 0
for i in range(1, 4):
    total = total + i
print(total)

total = 0
for i in range(1, 4):
    total += i
print(total)

title: Data Structures
description: Master Python data collections including lists, list methods, and key-value dictionaries.

missions.title: List Mutation
missions.description: Add new items to the end of a list using append().
missions.objective: Create fruits = ["apple"]. Call fruits.append("banana"), then print fruits.
hints:
Write:
fruits = ["apple"]
fruits.append("banana")
print(fruits)

missions.title: Dictionary Lookups Quiz
missions.description: Understand key-value retrieval in dictionaries.
missions.objective: Given user = {"name": "Zayir"}, how do you access the value "Zayir"?
hints: Use square bracket notation with the string key 'name'.

missions.title: Dictionary Creation
missions.description: Store key-value pairs using Python dictionaries.
missions.objective: Create person = {"role": "Developer"}. Print person["role"].

missions.title: List Pop Fill-In
missions.description: Remove the last item from a list.
missions.objective: Fill in the missing method name to remove the last item from numbers.
hints: The method to remove and return the last list item is pop.

missions.title: List Indexing
missions.description: Retrieve specific elements by zero-based index.
missions.objective: Create colors = ["red", "green", "blue"]. Print the second element ("green").
hints: In zero-based indexing, the second element is at index 1.

Write:
colors = ["red", "green", "blue"]
print(colors[1])

title: Functions & Scope
description: Master modular programming using custom functions, parameters, return values, and built-ins like len() and type().

missions.title: Defining Functions
missions.description: Functions let you group reusable blocks of code using the def keyword.
missions.objective: Define a function named greet() that prints "Hello!", then call greet().
hints:
Write:
def greet():
    print("Hello!")

greet()

missions.title: Function Parameters Quiz
missions.description: Understand how arguments are passed into function parameters.
missions.objective: What is the correct syntax to define a function double that accepts parameter x?
hints: Parameters go inside the parentheses after the function name.

missions.title: Return Values
missions.description: Functions return calculated outputs back to the caller using return.
missions.objective: Define a function add(a, b) that returns a + b. Print the output of add(3, 4).
hints:
Write:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

print(add(3, 4))

missions.title: The len() Built-In
missions.description: Use len() to measure string length or collection item count.
missions.objective: Fill in the missing function name to measure length of items = [10, 20, 30].
hints: The built-in function to measure length is len.

missions.title: Built-in Type Inspector
missions.description: Check variable data types dynamically using type().
missions.objective: Create message = "Forge". Print type(message).
hints:
Write:
message = "Forge"
print(type(message))

title: Object-Oriented Programming
description: Learn OOP principles by creating custom classes, instantiating objects, assigning attributes, and defining instance methods.

missions.title: Defining Classes
missions.description: Classes serve as blueprints for creating custom object instances using the class keyword.
missions.objective: Define an empty class named Car using pass, then instantiate c = Car().
hints:
Write:
class Car:
    pass

c = Car()

missions.title: Class Instance Quiz
missions.description: Understand how object instances are created in Python.
missions.objective: Given class Dog:, how do you create a new instance of Dog?
hints: Call the class name with parentheses, e.g. my_dog = Dog()

missions.title: Instance Attributes
missions.description: Assign dynamic data attributes to instances using dot notation.
missions.objective: Create an instance p = Person(). Set p.name = "Alice", then print p.name.
hints:
Write:
class Person:
    pass

p = Person()
p.name = "Alice"
print(p.name)

validAnswers:
class Person:
    pass

p = Person()
p.name = "Alice"
print(p.name)

missions.title: Self Parameter Fill-In
missions.description: Instance methods in Python must take self as their first parameter.
missions.objective: Fill in the missing parameter keyword used in Python methods to reference the instance.
hints: The first parameter of a method in Python is conventionally named self.

missions.title: Instance Methods
missions.description: Define methods inside a class to provide behavior to objects.
missions.objective: Define class Player with a method speak(self) that prints "Ready". Instantiate p = Player() and call p.speak().
missions.starterCode: # Define Player class with speak method below

title: Error Handling & Exceptions
description: Master robust error handling using try-except blocks to catch division by zero, invalid value parsing, and missing keys.

missions.title: Try Except Basics
missions.description: Prevent program crashes caused by division by zero using try-except.
missions.objective: Write a try-except block that tries x = 10 / 0 and catches ZeroDivisionError to print "Cannot divide by zero".

missions.title: Exception Types Quiz
missions.description: Identify standard Python exceptions.
missions.objective: Which exception is raised when trying to convert string "abc" into an integer using int("abc")?
hints: Converting invalid string formats to numbers raises a ValueError.

missions.title: Catching ValueError
missions.description: Handle invalid data casting gracefully using ValueError.
missions.objective: Write a try-except block attempting num = int("xyz") and catching ValueError to print "Invalid number".

missions.title: KeyError Fill-In
missions.description: Handle missing dictionary key lookups.
missions.objective: Fill in the missing exception keyword to catch missing key lookups.
hints: Missing dictionary key lookups raise a KeyError.

missions.title: Generic Except Block
missions.description: Catch any unhandled exception using the generic Exception fallback.
missions.objective: Write a try-except block trying y = 5 / 0 and catching Exception to print "An error occurred".
